Executive Summary
01
This vertical launches StandardMeds NAD+ Therapy — a physician-prescribed injectable
NAD+ protocol sold as a longevity and cellular-energy program. The funnel is built around a
scored assessment called the NAD+ Scan, and Logicall handles two recoverable stages:
Score Abandon and Checkout Abandon.
Page 1 of 12

READ THIS FIRST — EVERY LEAD IN THIS VERTICAL IS A MAN
The NAD+ Scan disqualifies women on the second screen — the protocol, dosing and patient
education are built for male physiology. A woman who starts the scan never becomes a lead, so
every name on your call list is male. If a woman answers the phone, she is a spouse or family
member: do not discuss the patient's health, his assessment, or the product with her. Ask
for him by name, or offer to call back. This is a HIPAA line, not a preference.
STAGE PRIORITY — CHECKOUT ABANDON IS THE BIGGEST LEVER
The two stages don't carry the same weight. Checkout Abandon has the lowest volume but the
highest conversion ceiling: the lead already saw his score, clicked through to the protocol page,
saw the plans and the price, and stopped one click short. He's the closest to "yes" of any
segment here. Treat every Checkout Abandon call as priority.
IMPORTANT — QUIZ ABANDONMENT IS NOT RECOVERABLE
The NAD+ Scan is long — 47 screens — and captures name, email and phone on screen 45,
right before the score is calculated. If a lead drops before that, we have zero contact data.
There is no "Quiz Abandon" recovery. The recoverable stages start once a lead finishes the
scan and his score is generated.
The two recoverable stages
1. Score Abandon — finished the NAD+ Scan, saw his score and the "you're a strong
candidate" verdict, and never clicked through to the protocol page. (Pricing-passive call —
he hasn't seen a price yet. Your job is to get him to the plans.)
2. Checkout Abandon — reached the protocol page, saw the three plans and the price, didn't
complete the order. (Pricing-active call.)
ONE THING THAT MAKES THIS FUNNEL UNUSUAL — THE PRICE LIVES ON THE CHECKOUT
Unlike neuropathy, anti-aging (skin) or nail fungus, there is no separate plan-selection page
here. The score page has no prices on it at all; plan choice and payment both live on the
protocol/checkout page. So on a Score Abandon call the lead has never seen a number — don't
introduce one unless he asks. On a Checkout Abandon call he has seen all three.
What's different about this category
It's an injection, and that's the number-one objection. Weekly at-home subcutaneous
injections with a 31-gauge needle. Not a pill, not a cream. Expect needle hesitation on most
calls and lead with how small and fast it is.
Page 2 of 12

Nobody is sick. This isn't pain, ED or a visible nail problem — the motivation is energy,
mental clarity, and not feeling like a lesser version of himself. The score is the emotional
hook, not a symptom.
The score is a screening snapshot, not a diagnosis. The page says so in writing. You may
reference his score; you may never interpret it as a medical finding. See §5.
Highest price point in the portfolio. $199/mo at the entry tier. The 0% installment option is
your most useful tool on price — see §2.
The Product at a Glance
02
Read this card before your first call. Everything you'll anchor on lives here.
StandardMeds NAD+ Therapy
LONGEVITY · INJECTABLE · PHARMACEUTICAL-GRADE NAD+
A physician-prescribed, pharmaceutical-grade injectable NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine
dinucleotide) protocol, compounded by an FDA-registered US pharmacy and shipped as pre-
mixed vials with everything needed to self-administer at home.
MECHANISM NAD+ is a coenzyme present in every cell. It powers the mitochondria — the cell's
energy machinery — and supports DNA repair and cellular metabolism. NAD+ levels
fall roughly 50% by age 40 and keep declining. The protocol replenishes what the
body has stopped making.
WHY INJECT Peer-reviewed work published in Aging and Disease found oral NAD+ cannot
meaningfully raise NAD+ levels in plasma or tissue — the digestive system breaks
the molecule down first. Injection bypasses the gut entirely and delivers near-
complete absorption into the bloodstream. This is the answer to "why not just
take a pill?"
PROTOCOL Typically one or two injections per week, about ten seconds each, with a 31-
gauge needle — among the smallest made. Dosing is set by the StandardMeds
physician per patient; there is no fixed dose to quote.
SHIPS WITH Pre-mixed pharmaceutical-grade NAD+, sterile alcohol swabs, 31-gauge syringes,
and step-by-step instructions. Packed on ice, shipped discreetly, typically within 24
hours of physician approval.
Page 3 of 12

NOT A Prescription-only, compounded per patient by an FDA-registered pharmacy after a
SUPPLEMENT physician reviews the assessment. Worth saying out loud — many leads assume it's
the same category as the NAD/NMN capsules sold online.
AUDIENCE Men. Dosing, protocol and patient education are optimized for male physiology, and
the scan disqualifies women up front.
TONE Peer-to-peer, no hype, faintly clinical. These leads self-identify as taking their health
seriously. "You already did the scan — this is the protocol that acts on it."

Anchor on the six-month, step down to the three. The three-month is the shortest window clinicians
consider meaningful for cellular-age change, and it's what the page pre-selects and badges "Most Popular" —
plenty of leads land there, and that's a good sale. But the six-month is the "full cellular reset" tier, the lowest
per-month price we have, and it saves $300. If six months is more than he wants to commit to, the three-month
is your step-down. Never push a lead down to the one-month unless he asks — it's the highest per-month price
on the board.
YOUR BEST TOOL ON PRICE — 0% INSTALLMENTS
The three-month and six-month plans both offer 0% installments spread over 12 months.
That turns $894 into a manageable monthly number without discounting anything. When a lead
balks at the total, reach for this before you reach for a shorter plan — it protects the sale and
the tier.
EVERY PLAN INCLUDES THE SAME PROGRAM
Page 4 of 12

Clinician review of his NAD+ Score, a custom protocol, medication shipped to his door, ongoing
clinical support and dose adjustments, free dosage increases, unlimited free doctor consults,
24/7 support, free expedited shipping, and the home injection kit. Also worth knowing:
HSA/FSA eligible, cancel anytime, and the price is the same at every dosage level — a higher
dose does not cost more.
OFFERS MAY VARY OVER TIME
Standard Meds continuously tests and rotates offers, so a lead may see plans or prices
different from the ones above. The live protocol/checkout page is always the source of truth.
Per-Stage Playbook
03
Two stages, two cards. Openers and discovery questions are a guide, not a script to read
verbatim — adjust to your own voice. These leads went through a 47-screen assessment about
their own decline; treat that investment with respect.
STAGE 1 OF 2
Score Abandon
The lead finished the whole NAD+ Scan, got his score — a battery percentage, a biological age
against his real age, a risk reading — and the page told him he's a strong candidate for the
protocol. Then he left without clicking through. He is invested but unpriced: he spent real time,
got a result that named something he already suspected, and never found out what it costs.
Your job on this call is not to sell a plan. It's to get him back to the page that shows them.
GOAL
Send his results link via SMS
AVG CALL
≤ 5 min
PRICING POSTURE
Passive — he hasn't seen a price
OPENER (≤ 15 SEC)
"Hi {first name}, this is {agent name} calling from Standard Meds. You completed the
NAD+ Scan recently and your results came back — I saw you didn't get a chance to go
through them. I wanted to check in — is this a good time for a quick call?"
Page 5 of 12

DISCOVERY QUESTION (≤ 45 SEC)
"You got all the way through the scan, which most people don't — was there something in
the results that didn't make sense, or did life just get in the way?"
ADDRESS — MOST COMMON PATTERNS
"I don't remember doing that" / "what was it again?" → very common on a long
assessment. Re-anchor in one sentence: "it's the assessment that scores your
cellular energy and estimates your biological age against your real age — you
finished it and came out as a candidate for the NAD+ protocol."
"What is NAD+?" → the mitochondria line from §2, short. Then stop. Long
explanations lose this call; the page does the explaining.
"What does it cost?" → he's entitled to know, so answer straight and anchor: "the
six-month protocol works out to a hundred forty-nine a month, and there's a zero-
percent installment option that spreads it over twelve months. The plans are all laid
out on your results page — can I text it to you?"
"Is it a pill?" → don't dodge it. "It's a small weekly injection you do at home — thirty-
one gauge needle, about ten seconds. That's specifically why it works where the pills
and powders don't."
"I need to think about it" → acknowledge, send the link, get off the phone. He
hasn't seen the offer yet; there's nothing to close.
CLOSE
"Can I text you the link to your results right now so you can see where you landed
and what the protocol looks like? Takes a minute."
ACTION ON YES
Trigger SMS send with his personalized results link from the recovery system — not a
generic page URL. A generic link opens in sample mode and shows a stranger's score,
which reads as broken. Confirm verbally: "Sent — you should see the text any moment.
Let me know when it comes through."
VOICEMAIL SCRIPT
"Hi {first name}, this is {agent name} from Standard Meds. You completed the NAD+
Scan recently and your results are ready — I just wanted to make sure you'd seen them. I'll
send a text with your link so you can look when it's convenient. Take care!"
Page 6 of 12

STAGE 2 OF 2 · HIGHEST PRIORITY
Checkout Abandon
Lower volume than Score Abandon but the single highest-conversion call in the playbook. The
lead read his results, clicked through to the protocol page, saw all three plans and the price, and
stopped before ordering. He is fully informed. Something specific stopped him — usually the
total, the needle, or "let me think about it." Don't re-explain NAD+. Find the one thing and
remove it.
GOAL
Send his checkout link via SMS
AVG CALL
≤ 5 min, ideally < 3
PRICING POSTURE
Active — hold the tier, offer installments
OPENER (≤ 15 SEC)
"Hi {first name}, this is {agent name} calling from Standard Meds. You went through the
NAD+ Scan and got as far as picking your protocol but didn't finish up — I wanted to check
in and see if anything came up. Is this a good time?"
DISCOVERY QUESTION (≤ 45 SEC)
"You were right at the last step — was it the price, a question about the injections, or
something else I can help with?"
ADDRESS — MOST COMMON PATTERNS
The total → installments first, always. "You don't have to pay it up front — the six-
month runs on zero-percent installments over twelve months." Only step down to the
three-month if he closes the door on the six.
The needle → smallest gauge made, ten seconds, cold pack beforehand kills most of
the sensation, kit and instructions included, and the medical team walks him through
the first one.
"Will it actually work for me?" → don't promise. Point at the structure: a licensed
physician reviews his profile before prescribing, dose adjustments are free and
ongoing, and he can cancel anytime. The program adapts; it isn't one shot in the
dark.
Page 7 of 12

Payment friction / "card was declined" → reassure, suggest another card, mention
the link takes him straight back to the same page with his plan still selected.
"Let me think" → acknowledge, offer the link, nothing is lost. One re-offer, then end.
TANGIBLE ANCHORS (USE WHEN PRICE COMES UP)
NAD+ THERAPY — ANCHOR ANGLES
Six-month at $149/mo vs one-month at $199/mo — $300 saved, and it's the full reset window
rather than a trial
0% installments over 12 months — the total stops being the obstacle
An IV NAD+ drip at a clinic is a single appointment at clinic pricing, and requires going there
every time; this is a home protocol with a physician attached
Oral NAD/NMN capsules cost real money every month and, per the research, don't raise tissue
levels at all
Unlimited doctor consults, free dosage increases, expedited shipping and the injection kit are
all included — and HSA/FSA funds can be used
CLOSE
"Can I send you the link right now so you can pick up where you left off? Takes a
minute."
ACTION ON YES
Trigger SMS send with the checkout link for the plan he had selected. Confirm
verbally: "Sent — you should see the text any moment. Let me know when it comes
through."
VOICEMAIL SCRIPT
"Hi {first name}, this is {agent name} from Standard Meds. You were almost finished
setting up your NAD+ protocol and I wanted to check whether you had any questions. I'll
send a text with your link so you can pick it back up. Take care!"
Objection Library
04
The full bench of rebuttals — guidance, not scripts to read verbatim. When a question turns
medical (his dose, his kidneys or liver, a drug he's taking, whether his score means something
is wrong with him), defer to the physician review — do not advise.
Page 8 of 12

Q "What is NAD+, in plain English?"
A "It's a coenzyme that sits in every cell in your body, and its main job is powering the mitochondria —
the part of the cell that makes your energy. It also supports DNA repair. The catch is that your levels drop
about fifty percent by age forty and keep falling from there. The protocol replenishes what your body has
stopped making on its own."
Q "Why can't I just take a pill or a powder?"
A "Because it doesn't survive the trip. Peer-reviewed research in Aging and Disease found that oral
NAD+ can't meaningfully raise the levels in your blood or your tissue — your digestive system breaks the
molecule down before it gets anywhere. The injection bypasses the gut completely, so you get close to
full absorption. That's the entire reason this is delivered the way it is."
Q "I hate needles." / "Does it hurt?"
A "Completely fair, and it's the first thing most guys say. It's a thirty-one gauge needle — about as thin
as they make — and the injection takes roughly ten seconds. Most patients report little to nothing. If
you're sensitive, a cold pack on the spot for a minute beforehand takes care of most of it. The kit and the
instructions come with it, and the medical team will walk you through your first one."
Q "How often would I have to do this?"
A "Most patients are once or twice a week, ten seconds each. Your exact protocol gets set by the
StandardMeds physician based on your profile and your goals — I can't set your dose, that's his call after
the review."
Q "Is it safe?"
A "NAD+ is a molecule your body already makes, so the protocol is replenishing something that's
declining rather than introducing something foreign. Every protocol is supervised by a board-certified
physician and nothing is prescribed until he's reviewed your full medical profile — that review is exactly
where safety gets confirmed for you specifically."
Q "Is this FDA approved?"
A "It's compounded by FDA-registered US pharmacies and it's prescription-only — it isn't a supplement.
Each order is prepared for the individual patient based on the protocol his physician approved."
Q "Are there side effects?"
A "It's well tolerated by most patients. Some men feel mild warmth, a flush, or a brief light-headedness
on the first dose as the body adjusts, and that usually passes within minutes. Your physician goes
through the full list with you during the medical consult."
Q "How fast will I notice anything?"
A "A lot of patients report clearer thinking, better energy and better sleep within the first days. The
deeper changes — body composition, blood markers, biological age — build over weeks and months of
staying consistent. I'd rather set that expectation honestly than oversell you the first week."
Q "$199 a month is a lot." / "It's expensive."
Page 9 of 12

A "I hear you, and there are two things worth knowing. First, the longer protocols bring the monthly down
a long way — the six-month is a hundred forty-nine a month, three hundred dollars less overall. Second,
you don't have to pay it up front: there's a zero-percent installment option that spreads it over twelve
months. And the price covers the whole program — the consults, the dose adjustments, the shipping, the
kit — not just the medication."
Q "Which plan should I pick?"
A "The six-month is what I'd point you at. It's the full reset window, it's the lowest per-month price at a
hundred forty-nine, and it saves you three hundred. The three-month at a hundred sixty-nine is the
shortest window clinicians consider meaningful, so it's a solid starting point if six months is more than
you want to lock in. The single month is the most expensive way to buy it per-month, so I'd only go there
if you specifically want to try one before committing."
Q "Does insurance cover it?"
A "It's a cash-pay compounded telehealth program, so it doesn't bill insurance — but it is HSA and FSA
eligible, so if you've got funds sitting in one of those you can use them."
Q "Can I cancel? Am I locked in?"
A "No contracts and no lock-in. You can pause, skip or cancel future shipments any time from your
patient account."
Q "What does my score actually mean? Am I unhealthy?"
A "I want to be careful here, because the scan is an educational screening snapshot based on what you
reported — it isn't a medical diagnosis, and I'm not a clinician. What it does tell us is that you came out
as a candidate for the protocol. The licensed physician reviews your full profile and he's the one who
tells you what it means for you."
Q "I want to run it by my own doctor first."
A "Of course, and a licensed physician is already part of this — he reviews your assessment before
anything is approved and will flag anything that isn't a fit. If it helps, I'll text you the link so you've got the
details in front of you for that conversation."
Q "I'm on other medication / I have kidney or liver problems — can I do this?"
A "That's an important question and it's exactly what the physician reviews in your assessment before
anything is approved. I'm not able to give medical advice on it, but the review is built to catch it."
Q "Is this just for men?"
A "The protocol, the dosing and the guidance are built specifically for male physiology, so the program is
set up for men. If you're asking on behalf of someone else, I'd point them at our team rather than guess."
Compliance & Operational Rules
05
Page 10 of 12

The universal rules from your first Standard Meds playbook still apply in full — TCPA window,
self-identification, recording disclosure, opt-out, no invented discounts, no claiming approval
before physician review, no link-send to voicemail. This section covers only what is different or
elevated for NAD+.
#1 RULE — THE SCORE IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS, AND YOU ARE NOT CLINICAL
The results page states in writing that the NAD+ Score is an educational screening snapshot
based on self-reported answers, not a medical diagnosis. You may reference that a lead
completed the scan and came out a candidate. You may never tell him his cells are damaged,
that his biological age means he is ill, that he is deficient in NAD+, or what his numbers mean
clinically. Every interpretation question routes to one answer: "the physician reviews that with
you."
New or elevated for NAD+
Never coach the injection
Do not explain technique, sites, depth, or what to do if something goes wrong. You may say it's
subcutaneous, weekly, 31-gauge, ten seconds, kit included. Anything past that is the medical team's.
Never set or discuss a dose
Dosing is set by the physician per patient, and the price is the same at every level. If he asks "how much
will I be on" — "your physician sets that after the review."
Never clear a medical condition
This assessment screens for G6PD deficiency, chronic kidney disease, cirrhosis and current medications
because the pharmacy requires it. If a lead raises any of them, do not reassure — route to the physician
review. A wrong "you'll be fine" here is a safety event.
Never promise biological-age reduction
No "this will take five years off your cells." Energy, clarity and sleep in the first days, deeper change over
weeks and months — that's the honest frame, and it's the one in §2.
Never build a pitch on the countdown
Both the results page and the checkout run reservation timers. Don't use them as urgency. If you need
urgency, use the real thing: NAD+ keeps declining while he waits.
Men only — and mind who answers
Page 11 of 12

Every lead is male. If a woman answers, she's a spouse or family member: ask for him by name or offer a
callback. Do not discuss his health, his assessment or the product with her. HIPAA line.
Reach for installments before a smaller plan
0% over 12 months is on the page — it isn't a discount you're inventing, and it saves the tier. Downgrade
only when he has closed the door.
Respect the 47 screens
These leads answered dozens of uncomfortable questions about their own decline. Peer-to-peer and
unhurried, never salesy. Cheerful hype reads as insulting on this call.
